title: Pool of Radiance
build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

records.c: The 6510's data direction register. receive_block's BIT $00 is only there to spend three cycles.
The 6510's port: bits 0-2 choose what shows at $A000, $D000 and $E000. The engine switches the KERNAL out to reach the RAM beneath it, and the I/O area out to write the character set at $D000.
fast_load's copy of $DD00 with only the VIC bank bits (0-1): receive_block writes it to release the serial lines and ORs $10 into it to pull CLOCK.
The string pointer, low byte: print_string ($2D28) prints the zero-terminated string at ($07/$08), and the printing routines point it at what they print.

The item pointer, low byte: item_slot_ptr points ($3B/$3C) at an item in the working character's second page, item_type_ptr at an item type's entry in ITEMS ($7B00).
The item pointer, high byte.
The character pointer, low byte: char_page_ptrs points ($3F/$40) at a character slot's first page ($4D00 + 256 times the slot).

The party entry pointer, high byte.

A row counter: decode_string's character count ($FF ends), and the row scroll_window copies into.
The KERNAL's message switch: view_init sets it to 0, which turns the KERNAL's messages off.
The sprite routines' pointer, low byte: a picture header at $EA00 + $40 per entry (find_sprite_picture, draw_monster_sprites).
The sprite routines' pointer, high byte.
The low byte of the KERNAL's jiffy clock, which goes up every interrupt: frame_delay times the portrait animation by it.
The colour RAM row pointer, low byte: row_address points ($A3/$A4) at the colour RAM of the row it finds on the text screen, and put_char stores the colour there.
The colour RAM row pointer, high byte.
A second general pointer, low byte: the unpacker's destination, the string decode_string writes, the second of the two strings COMPARE compares, the wall characters renumber_wall_chars changes.

A third pointer, low byte: the first of the two strings COMPARE compares, and the colour RAM row scroll_window copies from.
The third pointer, high byte.

The KERNAL's end-of-load pointer, low byte: fast_load's destination, which it returns as the end of the file.
The end-of-load pointer, high byte.
A counter many routines borrow: a loop count, a figure being compared, a column.
A second borrowed counter: delay's outer count, a row, a figure being taken away.
The sound driver's own zero page, $B2-$B9, swapped in from $BA08 while it runs: the three streams' read pointers ($B2/$B3, $B4/$B5, $B6/$B7) and the sound data's base ($B8/$B9).
The high byte of stream 0's read pointer.
The KERNAL's file name length: fast_load sends that many bytes of the name.
The low byte of the sound data's base while the driver runs.
The KERNAL's secondary address: fast_load puts a file at its own load address when it is not 0. While the sound driver runs, the high byte of the sound data's base.
The KERNAL's device number, the drive listen_command and drive_init talk to.
The KERNAL's file name pointer, low byte ($BB/$BC), which fast_load reads the name from.
The KERNAL's load address, low byte ($C3/$C4): where fast_load puts a file when the secondary address is 0.
The KERNAL's load address, high byte.
The number of keys in the KERNAL's keyboard buffer: read_input takes the first key waiting and sets it to 0, which throws away any others.

The direction last walked outdoors, 0-7 from north round clockwise: overland_icons picks the party marker's picture by it, over four.

The linker, the game's top loop. Loads the module whose number is at $6E11 (0 GEN, 1 DUNGEON, 2 COMBAT, 3 INIT, 4 COM.PREP, 5 POST.COM, 8 FINAL, 9 CAMP; 6 and 7 have no file) to $0800 with load_file ($2FC7), its name and length from the tables at $2BBB-$2C07, asking for another disk side through disk_prompt ($4378) until the load succeeds, then calls the module at $0800 and loops when it returns. A negative module number calls $3BF0 and stops on a BRK. Before each load it calls $3BF7 and $487E, and clears the message delay $03FC.

The modules' file names run together: GEN, DUNGEON, COMBAT, INIT, COM.PREP, POST.COM, "@" and "@" for modules 6 and 7, which have no file, FINAL and CAMP. The linker ($2B80) takes each name's length from $2BEA, its low byte from $2BF4 and its high byte from $2BFE, indexed by the module number.
Length of each module's file name, by module number 0-9 (3 GEN ... 4 CAMP), read by the linker ($2B80).
Low byte of each module's file name in module_names ($2BBB), by module number, read by the linker ($2B80).
High byte of each module's file name ($2B for all ten), read by the linker ($2B80).
Fourteen bytes that no file loads and nothing reads by address, between the linker's tables and the resource end addresses; they keep the memory's power-on pattern.

The end address of the file each of the 25 resource slots last loaded, low bytes, written by load_resource ($4222) and read when a later load decides which slots it has spoiled. No file loads here: the table starts as the memory's power-on pattern.
The high bytes of the resource slots' end addresses (resource_end_lo, $2C16).
LIBRARY's jump table: thirty JMPs the modules call at fixed addresses, so a module need not know where each routine is. $2C84-$2C86 are three NOPs in place of an entry.

The rest of LIBRARY's jump table, after the three NOPs at $2C84: read_input, input_number ($2F36), input_line, the current module's own entry at $0803, load_character from $6DB1, store_character, load_party_entry, store_party_entry, text_screen and compute_combat_stats.

Scrolls the text window ($03F2-$03F5) up one row from its top row ($03F4): copies each row's characters and colours from the row below, blanks the bottom row with spaces and moves the cursor row ($03CD) up one, not below 0. $2CA8 does the same from the row in X.

A = a screen row: sets $4C/$4D to that row's address on the text screen (row*40 plus the screen's page at $0288) and $A3/$A4 to its address in colour RAM ($D800). Returns the screen address low in A, high in X. Uses multiply ($2E30).
Points $4E/$4F at the screen row of the cursor ($03CD); $2D1A takes the row in A.
cursor_row_address for the row in A rather than the cursor's.
Prints the zero-terminated string at ($07/$08) at row A, column Y: stores them as the cursor ($03CD, $03CC) and falls into print_string ($2D28).

Prints the zero-terminated string at ($07/$08) at the cursor ($03CC column, $03CD row) in the colour at $0286, at most $03F6 characters. Wraps to the next row through newline ($3ECB) at the window's right edge ($03F3) and scrolls the window ($2CA5) at its bottom ($03F5). Each character is ANDed with $BF, which turns the upper-case letters' codes into screen codes. With a message delay at $03FC, it waits that long after each character (the typing speed). Leaves the cursor after the string and ($07) past it.

The random-number generator: six rounds of a lagged sum over the six bytes $03C2-$03C7 (the newest is the sum of itself, $03C6, $03C7 and one, and the others shift along), adding each round's new byte into $03C8. Returns that sum in A and X.

Y = a limit: returns a random number from 0 to Y in A and X (0 at once when Y is 0). Masks random ($2D88) with the smallest all-ones mask that covers Y (table $2DEC) and draws again until the result is not above Y. Carry clear.
Y = a number of sides: returns a roll from 1 to Y in A (and $03C8), X one more than random_to's result. $2DE1 rolls 1 to Y+1.
roll_die without its first DEY: a roll from 1 to Y+1.
The masks 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255 that random_to ($2DBC) chooses from by the highest set bit of its limit.

Clears the text window from row A to its bottom ($03F5), each row from the right edge ($03F3) back to the left edge ($03F2), with spaces in the current colour. $2E14 clears from row 20, the message area; $2E19 clears the whole window from its top row ($03F4).
clear_rows from the text window's top row ($03F4): blanks the whole window.
Waits A+1 times about 65,000 loop passes (an inner count in Y inside a count of $FF in X); $2E21 starts with A already in $B1, and $2E23 with X already set (print_string's per-character delay).
Multiplies A by X, eight bits by eight: returns the 16-bit product in $4C (low, also in A) and $4D (high, also in X), carry clear.

Reads the joystick in port 2 ($DC00, low five bits, into $03F0) and takes one key from the KERNAL's keyboard buffer: the key into $03CB and A, with the buffer emptied ($C6 = 0), or $FF when no key is waiting. The game takes one key at a time this way.
Empties the keyboard buffer and waits for a key or a joystick movement (any of $03F0's bits clear) through read_input ($2E4E). Returns the key, or $FF when it was the joystick.

Reads a typed line of at most A characters into the buffer at $9700 (cleared first, 40 bytes) at the cursor, showing a cursor character ($1C) after the text. DEL ($14) rubs out the last character, RETURN ends it with a zero. With $03B6 negative only the digits 0-9 are taken (check_digit, $2EEE). The length is left in $03B7.
For input_line ($2E81): when $03B6 is negative (a number is wanted) returns X = 0 for a digit 0-9 and X = $FF for anything else; otherwise returns at once.
Stores A at ($4C),Y on the text screen and the current colour ($0286) at ($A3),Y in colour RAM. Keeps A.
Prints the signed byte A with a sign in front: "-" (print_char, $3217) and its magnitude for a negative, "+" for the rest, through print_number ($2F29).

Prints the number A (X and Y the higher bytes: $2F2B takes A and X, $2F2D A, X and Y, a 24-bit number) in decimal at the cursor. Divides by the powers of ten in $2FAF by repeated subtraction into the digits at $03D0, drops the leading zeros and prints them with print_string ($2D28).
print_number for the 16-bit number in A (low) and X (high), clearing Y.
print_number for the 24-bit number in A, X and Y, low byte first.
1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000 and 10000000 as three-byte little-endian numbers, for print_number ($2F29).

Loads a file through the KERNAL (SETLFS with device $038E and secondary address 0, SETNAM, LOAD) to the address in X (low) and Y (high), A being the name's length and the name's address the operands at $301C/$301E. The fast loader FAST1.O sits in the KERNAL's load vector. Stores the end address the KERNAL returns in $6D56/$6D57, calls $3F3A (the drive's status) and closes all files. Returns the status in $03F1 in A: zero when the load worked.

Saves memory from the address in $03EE/$03EF up to the address in X (low) and Y (high) through the KERNAL (SETLFS with device $038E and secondary address $FF, SETNAM through set_name, SAVE with the start pointer copied to $FD/$FE), A being the name's length. Calls $3F49 (the drive's status) and closes all files; returns the status in $03F1 in A.
Calls the KERNAL's SETNAM with the length in A and the name's address in its own LDX and LDY operands ($301C low, $301E high), which the callers rewrite before each load or save.
The low byte of the file name's address, which the linker ($2B9A) and load_resource_file ($40C8) write before calling load_file.
The high byte of the file name's address, written by the linker ($2BA0) and load_resource_file ($40CE).
Keeps A, X and Y in $03DE, $03DF and $03E0; $302C gets them back.
Gets A, X and Y back from $03DE, $03DF and $03E0, where save_regs put them.
Opens the command channel (secondary address 15) of drive $038E with the name set_name ($301B) points at as the command, then calls $3F5B and closes all files. Returns $03F1.
Fills memory from X (low) and Y (high) up to the address in $03EE/$03EF with A.

Turns the last input into a menu step. Keys "<", "," and cursor up, and the joystick up, step back (direction 0); ">", ".", cursor down and the joystick down step on (1); cursor right and the joystick right go right (2); cursor left and the joystick left go left (3). In a vertical menu ($6E94 = 0) steps 0 and 1 move the highlight $6EE6 up and down, wrapping at the $6E93 items; in a horizontal one steps 3 and 2 do; either way with a short pause, and the other directions return the key with carry clear. RETURN or fire returns the highlighted item's key from $6E96 indexed by $6EE6, carry set (fire after a pause); the left-arrow key, or the joystick held down and right with fire, returns $FF with carry set (leave the menu). Any other key comes back in A with carry clear. The direction is left in $6E95.
A = a character's slot: points $3F/$40 at its first page of 256 bytes ($4D00 + 256 times the slot) and $4C/$4D at its second ($5900 + 256 times the slot).
A = a party position: points $41/$42 at its 32-byte entry in the party table at $8300 ($8300 + 32 times the position) and keeps the position in $6DAA.
Copies character A's two pages (or, from $315D, the slot already in $6DB1) into the working copy at $6B00 and $6C20.
load_character for the slot already in $6DB1.
Copies the working character at $6B00 and $6C20 back to its slot $6DB1.
Copies party position $6DB4's 32-byte entry from $8300 into $6C00.
Copies the 32-byte entry at $6C00 back to party position $6DB4.

Prints the working character's name ($6B00) at row A, column Y; $34C3 at the cursor. The name is yellow when the party entry's flag ($6C0C bit 0) is set and cyan when it is not (only when the text colour is 3 or above); the colour goes back to $6E34 after.

The character screen's top half: clears the window, calls $488B, prints the name, then (white) the gender (message 8 + $6BD6), the race (message race-1 from $6B72, MONSTER for 0), AGE and the age ($6B74/$6B75), the alignment (message 18 + $6BD8), the class (print_class), the six abilities from $6B14-$6B19 with STR's percentage ($6B1A) in brackets when strength is 18, LEVEL ($6BA0) and EXP ($6BE8-$6BEA), HITPOINTS, then the money through $3B77. Keeps the row after the abilities in $48F0.
show_character without clearing the window first; the adventure module's unused_show_sheet ($0D51) enters here.
Rolls A dice of X sides ($6DB8 the count, $6DB9 the sides) through roll_die ($2DE0) and returns the 16-bit total in A (low) and X (high), also in $4C/$4D.
Points $3B/$3C at the working character's item $6DAD, one of sixteen 16-byte entries in its second page ($6C20 + 16 times the item).
Copies item A (or, from $3607, item $6DAD) of the working character into $6D7C, 16 bytes; $3615 store_item copies it back.
load_item for the item number in $6DAD.
Copies the item in hand ($6D7C, 16 bytes) back to the working character's slot $6DAD.
Points $3B/$3C at item type $6DAC's 16-byte entry in the item table ITEMS at $7B00.
Copies the type entry of the working item (its first byte, $6D7C, or A from $3640) from ITEMS ($7B00) into $6D8C, 16 bytes.
load_item_type for the item type in A.

One signed adjustment for each ability score 0-30 (-3 at 1-3 down to 0 at 8-16, up to +7 at 30), read by compute_combat_stats ($3729) with the score in X into $6DE8, which is added to the 60-minus-THAC0 figure ($6C0E).
A second signed adjustment for each ability score 0-30 (-2 at 1-2, 0 at 6-15, up to +14 at 30), read by compute_combat_stats ($3729) into $6DE7, which is added to the damage bonus ($6C17).

Works out the to-hit (60 minus THAC0, $6C0E) and the damage of the readied weapon (dice $6C13, sides $6C15, bonus $6C17) for the character in hand: from the character's base ($6B71), the weapon's own figures ($6D80 its magical plus, $6D95-$6D97, its flags $6D9A) and the strength adjustments ($6DE8, $6DE7), with a second readied item adding its plus again (bit 0 of the flags, $6DD7 or $6DD8). Does nothing without a readied weapon ($6DEA negative).
compute_combat_stats's unused first instruction, JSR load_character_slot ($315D): every one of the 34 calls in the modules enters at $3729, after it.

Builds the party entry's combat figures from the working character: damage dice ($6C13, from $6BDB-$6BE0), natural armour class ($6C0F, from $6BE1), movement ($6C1B, from $6B9F) and to-hit ($6C0E, from $6B71); dexterity's AC adjustment from $400D into $6DA1; the strength adjustments from $3651 and $3670 by strength index ($6BE2; index 0 when $6BE3 is clear), added straight to to-hit and damage when no weapon is readied. For a character ($6DB1 positive; a monster skips this) it then adds the weapon (weapon_bonuses, $368F) and each readied item's armour and speed (armour_move, armour_bonus); a magical armour's plus ($6DA6) cancels the bonus of a type-9 item ($6DA4). The front AC ($6C0F) is the better of armour and natural AC plus the four adjustments $6DA1-$6DA4; the rear AC ($6C10) leaves out dexterity and $6DA2 and is 2 worse.

For a readied item ($6D92 negative) adds its protection: a type-1 item's plus into $6DA2, an armour's base AC plus its magic into $6DA5 when it beats the best so far (type 2 also keeping its plus in $6DA6), a type-9 item's into $6DA4, any other's into $6DA3; and the item's $6D81 into $6DA7.

The character screen's lower half: the AC (60 minus $6C0F, through print_ac), the readied weapon and armour by name ($399B), the hit points ($6C19/$6C1A) at row 15, THACO (60 minus $6C0E), DAMAGE as dice, "D", sides and a signed bonus ($6C13, $6C15, $6C17), and the condition at row 22: message 41 plus the low three bits of $6C00, 1 OK to 7 STONED.

Scans the working character's sixteen items, last first, into the tables of what it carries: $6DE9 the lowest empty slot, $6DEA+type the readied item of each type below 9 ($FF where none), $6DF3 and $6DF4 two readied rings (type 9), $6DFA the list of filled slots ($6DF9 their number), $6DF5 the hands the readied items take ($6D8D each), $6DF6/$6DF7 the weight carried (each item's weight times its count, add_item_weight $4093, then one for every coin and gem), the readied weapon's $6D98 in $6D9C (and in $6D9D when its flags $6D9A have bit 3), and two particular items in $6DD7/$6DD8 (check_special_item $3982). A monster ($6DB1 negative) carries nothing.
For find_readied: remembers the item in hand ($6DAD) as $6DD7 when its type is $49, as $6DD8 when it is $1C.

Prints the item in hand's name at row A, column Y ($39A1 at the cursor): its count first ($6D86) when there is more than one, a "*" when it is magical and identified ($6DD9 and $6D80), then up to three words, each an index into the name table at $6F00/$7000 (ITEMNAMES), skipping those the item's flags ($6D82) hide.
print_item_name at the cursor.
The items screen: clears the window, prints the name at the top, EQUIPPED ITEM, then for each of the sixteen items carried a row with YES or NO for readied (bit 7 of $6D82) and its name.
Prints 60 minus A as a signed number: the game keeps armour class and THAC0 as 60 minus their value, so a better figure is a bigger byte.

Colours the menu item under the cursor ($6EE6) in the text colour ($6E34); $3A4D in the highlight colour ($03F8). Fills the item's width ($6ED2) of colour RAM from its column ($6EAA) on its row ($6EBE).
highlight_item in the highlight colour ($03F8): marks the menu choice under the cursor.

Shows the text screen: VIC bank 3 through CIA 2 ($DD00), screen at $CC00 and characters at $D000 ($D018 = $34), multicolour text on ($D016 bit 4), and tells the KERNAL the screen is at page $CC ($0288).

Not called: the same six switches as all_ram ($3AAB) and its partners, as GDRIVE has them at $C13D. $3A95 shows the character ROM at $D000 ($01 AND $FB), $3A9B puts I/O back, $3AA0 turns the KERNAL off ($01 AND $FD), $3AA6 back on.
Interrupts off, and all 64 KB RAM: clears the KERNAL and I/O bits of the processor port ($01 AND $F9, from the usual $36 to $30). $3AB1 sets them again and allows interrupts.

The weight a character carries before slowing, in coins, low bytes at $3AC1 and high bytes at $3AE0, by strength index ($6BE2, 0-30): nothing up to 11, 100 at 12-13, 200 at 14-15, 350, 500, 750 at 18, then 1000, 1250, 1500 and 2000 for the bands of exceptional strength, 3000 at 18/00, and 4500 to 15000 for 19-25: the Players Handbook's weight allowance.
The high bytes of the strength allowances (carry_allowance, $3AC1).

For a readied item of class 2 (armour): the character's movement ($6C1B) by the armour's weight ($6D84/$6D85): under 151 the base movement ($6B9F); 151 to 399, 9; 400 or more, 6; and a magical armour ($6D80 not zero) adds 3 to either of those.

Takes the strength allowance (carry_allowance, $3AC1) from the weight carried ($6DF6/$6DF7) into $48EE/$48EF, 0 when under it, and slows the character's movement ($6C1B) to 3 at 1024 coins over, 6 at 768, 9 at 512 (high byte 4, 3, 2), never raising it.

Lists the working character's money on the character screen, from the row in $48F0: for each of jewelry, gems, platinum, gold, electrum, silver and copper ($6BBB-$6BC8, two bytes each) that is not zero, its name (message from $3BCF) at column 11 and the number at column 20; the kinds shown go in $6D59 ($6D58 their count) for the menu that follows.
Message numbers of the seven kinds of money, copper (34) to gems (39) and jewelry (57).
Yellow text ($0286 = 7) when the hit points ($6C19/$6C1A) are not the full count ($6B76/$6B77).

The interrupt, through $0314: the KERNAL's own, from CIA 1's timer, 60 times a second on a PAL machine as on an NTSC one. Plays the sound driver's step (SOUNDFX at $BA00), then goes on into the KERNAL's handler at $EA31.

Sets bit 0 of the processor port, from $36 to $37, putting BASIC's ROM back at $A000; $3BF7 takes it out again. The linker does this before it stops the machine (BRK) for a negative module, and $4078 around a call to GDRIVE's $C003. Around draw_view the point is the switch that follows: GDRIVE's kernal_out ($C14F) clears bit 1, and from $37 that leaves $35, RAM at $E000 with the I/O chips still in.
Clears bit 0 of the processor port, from $37 back to $36: RAM at $A000 again.

For draw_box ($3C12): for each of the four sides, which of the four corner bytes give its start column and row ($3BFE, $3C02), its line character ($3C06: $1B across, $24 down) and the one-square steps ($3C0A, $3C0E) that keep the corners clear.
For each side of a box, which corner byte gives its start row (box_sides, $3BFE).
For each side of a box, its line character: $1B for the top and bottom, $24 for the sides.
For each side, the column step from its corner, -1, 0 or +1, that keeps the corners clear.
For each side, the row step from its corner, -1, 0 or +1.

Draws a frame in the box colour ($6E35): A and X point at four bytes, left column, top row, right column and bottom row, copied to $48F2. Fills each side with its line character through fill_rect ($3C7D), then sets the text colour back ($6E34).
Fills the screen from column $FB, row $FC to column $0378, row $0379 (either corner first: they are swapped into order) with the character in $48F6, through put_char ($2F02).

Prints a vertical menu and records its items for the menu keys: X and Y point at the item count, the column, the top row, then each item's zero-terminated text. Every item gets a row; its column ($6EAA), row ($6EBE), width ($6ED2) and number ($6E96) go in the menu tables and the count in $6E93.
Steps the pointer at $07/$08 on by one.
Steps the pointer at $07/$08 past the next zero-terminated string.

Prints a menu across the bottom row and records its items for the menu keys (a horizontal menu, $6E94 = 1): X and Y point at the item count, a heading, then each item's zero-terminated text. $3D53 shows every item; $3D55 only those whose bits are set in A and $48F9 (a 16-bit mask, first item lowest). Each item's column ($6EAA), row ($6EBE), width ($6ED2) and number ($6E96) go in the menu tables, one space apart, and the count in $6E93.
Copies the text window's edges ($03F2-$03F5: left, right, top, bottom) to $6E73; $3DD9 restore_window copies them back.
Copies the saved text window ($6E73) back to $03F2-$03F5 (save_window, $3DCD).
Blanks the bottom row (menu_window, then clear_window $2E19) and puts the text window back.
Sets the text window to the bottom row: columns 0 to 40, rows 24 to 25 (the four bytes at $3DFD).
The menu window's edges for menu_window ($3DF1): left 0, right 40, top 24, bottom 25.

Lists the party on the main screen, with the chosen member ($6D7B) in white; $3E06 without it. Prints the headings NAME and "AC HP" on row 2, then from row 4 one row for each of the eight party slots that is filled ($6C00 not zero), from the last to the first: the name in the text colour (red when bit 7 of $6C00 is set), the armour class right-aligned at column 34 and the hit points at column 36, yellow when wounded. Each row's slot goes in $6E36 and the number of rows in $6E3E; a choice beyond the last row goes back to the first.
Moves the cursor ($03CC) to the text window's left edge.

Turns the working character's strength ($6B14) and its percentage ($6B1A) into the index the strength tables use ($6BE2): the score itself up to 17; at 18, 18 plus one for each band the percentage reaches (1, 51, 76, 91, 100, the steps at $3EFF), so 18/00 is 23; above 18, the score plus 5, at most 30.
The steps of exceptional strength for strength_index ($3ED2), used from the last: 0, 51, 25, 15, 9, so the percentage passes them at 1, 51, 76, 91 and 100.
Divides the 16-bit number at $4C/$4D by A (low) and X (high), kept in $AB/$4B; $3F08 takes the divisor already there. Returns the quotient in $4C/$4D and in A and X, the remainder in $6E3F/$6E40.

After a load or save: when $6D9F is set, the result is the carry (0, or 62, the drive's FILE NOT FOUND); otherwise $3F49 reads the drive's error channel (file 15, secondary 15, no name) as two decimal digits into $03F1, reads the rest of the message away and closes it; $3F5B starts with the channel already open. $FF when the drive does not answer.
disk_status's own read: opens the drive's error channel and reads it (disk_status, $3F3A).
Reads the drive's error channel, already open as file 15, into $03F1: two decimal digits, the rest read away, then closes it; $FF when the drive does not answer. disk_command ($3046) calls it.
Sends the drive "I" on its command channel (LISTEN, secondary $6F), initialising the disk after a swap, then reads the error channel (disk_status).
Counts the filled party slots into $6E3E. The camp module calls it.

Searches the 64-entry table at $4900 (with its second column at $4940) from the last entry down for A; $3FE1 takes the second value from $6DB4, $3FE4 from X. An entry matches when its first byte is A and either A is 0, its second byte is negative, or its second byte equals X. Returns carry set and the entry's number in A and $6E78, or carry clear.
find_entry for the value in X.

The armour class adjustment for each dexterity 0-25, signed, in the game's 60-minus scale (plus is better): -4 at 1-3, -3, -2, -1 at 4-6, 0 at 7-13, then +1 at 14 and 15, +2 at 16, +3 at 17, +4 at 18-20, +5 at 21-23, +6 at 24-25. The rule book's table starts the bonus at 15; here 14 has it too.
Carry set when the party has item type A (with X, through find_entry $3FE4) or the working character carries it among its ten item numbers at $6BAD.
Records a vertical menu of A items over rows already printed: the items are numbered from 0, start at column X and row Y, one row each, and all reach the window's right edge ($03F3).

Calls GDRIVE's draw_view ($C003) with bit 0 of the processor port set (basic_in, $3BF0) and clears it after, so that draw_view's kernal_out gives $35: the walls and buffers under the KERNAL and the colour RAM both in reach.
Sets $6DD9 when find_entry ($3FE4) finds an entry 5 with any second value: whether items show as magical ("*", print_item_name).
Adds the item in hand's weight ($6D84/$6D85), times its count ($6D86) when it has one, to the weight carried ($6DF6/$6DF7).
Loads item $6DAD of the working character and its type entry (load_item, load_item_type).

Loads the file of resource slot X ($6D60; $40BC takes it there): puts the KERNAL's interrupt back (restore_irq, $487E), points load_file ($2FC7) at the slot's file name (resource_names, by $4209) and length ($4182), loads it to the slot's address ($41BE/$41D7), and on an error asks for the disk (disk_prompt, $4378) and tries again. Then $4871.

The twenty file names the engine loads, each ending in two hexadecimal digits that load_resource ($4222) overwrites with the number wanted: GDRIVE01, SQRPACI00, GEO00, SECSET00, SQRDATA00, PIC64, SPELLN00, SPELLE00, ECL00, WALLS00, SPRITE0C, ANIMATE00, MON00, BODY09, HEAD08, WALLSET00, WALLDEF00, CHARPIC00, COMPIC00, ITEMFILE00 (as they stand in this snapshot).
File name 1, SQRPACI: slot 1, loaded at $0400.
File name 2, GEO: slot 2, loaded at $0400.
File name 3, SECSET: slot 3, loaded at $6500.
File name 4, SQRDATA: slot 4, loaded at $8C00.
File name 5, PIC: slot 5, loaded at $8C00.
File name 6, SPELLN: slot 6, loaded at $AF00.
File name 7, SPELLE: slot 7, loaded at $A700.
File name 8, ECL: slot 8, loaded at $9900.
File name 9, WALLS: slot 9, loaded at $ED50.
File name 10, SPRITE: slot 10, loaded at $8400.
File name 11, WALLSET: slots 15, 16 and 17, loaded at $6650, $67E0 and $6970.
File name 12, WALLDEF: slots 18, 19 and 20, each loaded at $8C00.
File name 13, ANIMATE: slot 11, loaded at $8400.
File name 14, MON: slot 12, loaded at $6B00.
File name 15, BODY: slot 13, loaded at $8C00.
File name 16, HEAD: slot 14, loaded at $9000.
File name 17, CHARPIC: slots 21 and 22, loaded at $9900 and $8C00.
File name 18, COMPIC: slot 23, loaded at $8C00.
File name 19, ITEMFILE: slot 24, loaded at $9900.
The length of each of the twenty names; $4196 and $41AA their addresses, low and high.
The low bytes of the twenty resource file names' addresses.
The high bytes of the twenty resource file names' addresses.

For each of the 25 resource slots, where its file loads (low bytes at $41BE, high at $41D7): $C000 GDRIVE, $0400 SQRPACI and GEO, $6500 SECSET, $8C00 SQRDATA, PIC, BODY, WALLDEF and the pictures, $AF00 SPELLN, $A700 SPELLE, $9900 ECL, ITEMFILE and a CHARPIC, $ED50 WALLS, $8400 SPRITE and ANIMATE, $6B00 MON, $9000 HEAD, $6650, $67E0 and $6970 the three WALLSETs.
The high bytes of the resource slots' load addresses (resource_dest, $41BE).
For each slot, 1 when another load over its memory makes it stale, 0 for the three WALLDEFs (always reloaded), $FF ending the list at ITEMFILE.
For each of the 25 slots, which of the twenty names it loads: three slots share WALLSET, three WALLDEF, two CHARPIC.

Makes sure resource slot X holds file number A ($4222 reloads the number in $6E13): nothing for $FF or the number already there, and $7F only marks the slot as holding nothing. Otherwise writes the number in hexadecimal into the file name, loads it (load_resource_file), keeps its end ($6D56/$6D57) in $2C16/$2C2F, and marks with bit 7 of $6E13 every other slot whose memory the new file covered, so it loads again when next wanted. Carry set when it loaded.
load_resource for the file number in A, X the slot.

Asks for one of the party: prints the prompt at A (low) and X (high) on the bottom row, the party list with EXIT after it, and runs the menu with the cursor on the last choice ($6D61), each member in red when bit 7 of $6C00 is set. Returns the slot chosen in A ($6EFD), $FF for EXIT or the left arrow.

Asks for the disk after a failed load: waits for a key; then until the drive answers (drive_init, $3FB1) prints INSERT SIDE # with the side wanted ($6E12) and ", AND PRESS ANY KEY." on the bottom row and waits again. A key with $03F0 = 15 skips the prompt.
Prints the string at A (low) and X (high) on the bottom row, waits $49FC (the message speed) and clears it.
For a menu key with carry clear: up or down ($6E95 0 or 1) moves the chosen party member ($6D7B) and redraws the list, wrapping at the ends; returns carry clear. Other keys return as they came.
-1 and +1, the party cursor's step for up and down.
Loads party slot A ($6DB4) and its character: $4415 for the slot in $6DB4, $4418 only the character whose page is in the entry ($6C0D). $441E stores both back.
Loads the character whose page is in the party entry ($6C0D) as the working character.

The VIEW screen for the character in hand: frame, character sheet, combat figures and portrait, then the menu bar VIEW: ITEMS SPELLS TRADE DROP EXIT, offering those in the module's mask ($6EF7; the adventure module sets $11, ITEMS and EXIT) that apply (view_mask, $44AA), with the cursor on the last choice ($6EF9). ITEMS opens item_menu ($44CD); SPELLS, TRADE and DROP call routines a module patches in over the JSR $FFFF at $4470, $447A and $4480; EXIT or the left arrow returns.
The VIEW menu bar for menu_bar ($3D53): five items, heading "VIEW:", then ITEMS, SPELLS, TRADE, DROP and EXIT.

Narrows the VIEW mask in $6EF7 to what applies: no TRADE or DROP when bit 7 of $6BB8 is set or no money was listed ($6D58), no ITEMS when nothing is carried ($6DF9), no SPELLS when all 81 bytes of memorised spells ($6B20-$6B70) are zero.

The items screen: lists the items carried (show_items) with the menu bar of item actions (item_bar, $4511) under them; TRADE first asks for whom (trade_to, $4576) and comes back if the answer is EXIT; then the chosen action goes to pick_item ($4591). EXIT (item 8) or the left arrow returns.

Shows the item actions offered: the module's mask $6EF8 (the adventure module's $0D, READY, TRADE and DROP), none when nothing is carried, no HALVE with sixteen items, no TRADE or SELL when bit 7 of $6BB8 is set and the member's bit 7 of $6C00 is not; EXIT always. The cursor goes on the last choice ($6EFA).
The item menu bar: nine items, an empty heading, then READY, USE, TRADE, DROP, HALVE, JOIN, SELL, ID and EXIT.
Asks "TRADE TO ?" (the string at $4586) over the party list (choose_member, $42C6); the answer is in $6EFD.
"TRADE TO ?", the prompt over the party list for TRADE.

Puts a cursor on the item list for the action chosen ($6D62): the list from row 5, with EXIT after the last item. The item picked is loaded (load_item_full, $40B3) and handed to the action's routine (item_actions, $4611, patched into the JSR at $4605), then the combat figures are worked out again and the character stored, and the list shown again. EXIT or the left arrow returns.
The low byte of the action routine's address, written by pick_item ($45FC) from item_actions.
The high byte of the action routine's address, written by pick_item ($4602).
The routine for each item action, low bytes at $4611 and high at $4619: READY $4630, TRADE $4743, DROP $47DA; USE, HALVE, JOIN, SELL and ID are $FFFF here, for a module to fill in.
The high bytes of the item actions' routines (item_actions, $4611).
Keeps the item cursor ($6EFB) no further down than EXIT, the row after the last item ($6DF9).

READY: readies or puts away the item in hand. NOT HERE when the item can only be readied elsewhere (bit 7 of $6D8B) and $6DE4 is clear. A readied item is put away, unless it is cursed (bit 7 of $6D83): ITS CURSED. To ready one: WRONG CLASS unless the item's classes ($6D99) include the character's ($6BEB); TOO MANY OF THAT TYPE when one of its type (below 10) is readied already, two for rings (type 9); TOO MANY HANDS when its hands ($6D8D) and those in use ($6DF5) make three or more.
The messages of the item menus: ITS CURSED, WRONG CLASS, TOO MANY OF THAT TYPE, TOO MANY HANDS, CHARACTER OVERLOADED, "DROPPED ..." and NOT HERE.
Adds A (low) and X (high) to the weight carried ($6DF6/$6DF7); carry set when it overflows.
Adds A and X to the weight carried and returns carry set when it is still within the most the character can carry (max_load, $472E), carry clear when not or when the sum overflows.
The most the working character can carry: 1500 plus its strength's allowance (carry_allowance, $3AC1, by $6BE2), into $6D63/$6D64; returns the high byte in A.

TRADE: gives the item in hand to the member chosen ($6EFD). A readied item cannot be traded (not_readied, $48DB), so the cursed check after it never finds one. The item is kept at $6D45 while the receiver is loaded and its figures worked out; if it has sixteen items already or the weight would be too much (item_fits, $47A1), CHARACTER OVERLOADED and the giver is loaded back. Otherwise the item goes in the receiver's first empty slot ($6DE9), both are stored, and the giver's slot is emptied.

Carry clear when the kept item ($6D45) fits the character loaded: fewer than sixteen items, and its weight ($6D4D/$6D4E, times its count $6D4F when it has one) within the most it can carry (weight_fits).
Copies the item in hand ($6D7C, 16 bytes) to $6D45; $47CE takes it back.
Copies the kept item ($6D45, 16 bytes) back to the item in hand ($6D7C).

DROP: unless the item is readied (not_readied), shows "DROP YOUR" and the item's name under the character's name and asks DROP: NO YES on the bottom row. YES says "DROPPED ..." and empties the slot (item number 0).
The DROP menu bar: two items, heading "DROP: ", then NO and YES.
Draws the frame round the whole screen: draw_box ($3C12) with the corners at $4835, columns 0 to 39 and rows 0 to 23.
The edges draw_frame gives draw_box: left column 0, top row 0, right column 39, bottom row 23.

Sets the text window to columns 1-39, rows 1-23 (the four bytes at $4840); $4844 to rows 17-23 ($484B), the lower part; $484F to columns 17-39, rows 1-16 ($4856), right of the portrait. $485A copies the four bytes whose address is in A and X (patched into the LDA at $4862) and sets the longest line to 250 ($03F6).
window_main's edges, in set_window's order (left, right, top, bottom): columns 1-39, rows 1-23.
Sets the text window to columns 1-39, rows 17-23 (the bytes at $484B).
window_lower's edges: columns 1-39, rows 17-23.
Sets the text window to columns 17-39, rows 1-16 (the bytes at $4856), right of the portrait.
window_right's edges: columns 17-39, rows 1-16.
Copies the four window edges from the address in A (low) and X (high) to $03F2-$03F5, and sets the longest line to 250 ($03F6).
The low byte of the window edges' address, which set_window writes ($485A).
The high byte of the window edges' address, written by set_window ($485D).
Points the interrupt vector ($0314) at the game's own handler, irq ($3BEA), with the music; $487E restore_irq points it back at the KERNAL's ($EA31) for the KERNAL loader.
Points the interrupt vector back at the KERNAL's handler ($EA31), for the KERNAL's loader.
Moves the cursor to the text window's top row ($03F4) and left edge.
Turns 0-15 in A into its hexadecimal digit, "0"-"9" or "A"-"F".
Waits for a key or the joystick (wait_input, $2E6B) and hands it to menu_key ($306D).

When portraits are shown (bit 7 of $49FF) and $49EB is clear: makes sure the picture files are loaded (load_resource slot 11, then the head $6BFE in slot 14 and the body $6BFF in slot 13), draws the portrait's frame (the corners at $48D7, columns 27-39, rows 0-12) through the routine the module writes into the JSR at $48C7 (the adventure module's start writes $11BE there) and calls the sprite and animation entries $8406, $8403, $8409, $8403.
The low byte of the portrait frame routine's address, written by the module (the adventure module at $081C).
The high byte of the portrait frame routine's address, written by the module (at $0821).
The portrait frame's edges for draw_box (left, top, right, bottom): columns 27-39, rows 0-12.
Carry clear when the item in hand is not readied; for a readied one, shows message $33C5, EQUIPPED ITEM, and returns carry set.
Three zero bytes after not_readied that nothing reads by address.

The engine's working bytes: $48EE/$48EF the weight over the allowance, $48F0 the row after the abilities, $48F1 a loop count, $48F2-$48F5 a box's corners, $48F6 its line character, $48F7 a digit count, $48F8/$48F9 a menu's mask, $48FA an item number, $48FB a slot number.
The high byte of the weight over the allowance (load_move, $3B39).
The screen row after the abilities, where show_money starts the money.
A loop count: items left in a menu, sides left in a box.
A box's left column, then its top row, right column and bottom row in $48F3-$48F5 (draw_box).
A box's top row (draw_box).
A box's right column (draw_box).
A box's bottom row (draw_box).
The character fill_rect fills with: a box side's line character.
The digits left to read from the error channel (read_error_channel).
The low byte of a menu's item mask, shifted one bit for each item.
The high byte of a menu's item mask.
The number of the menu item being built.
The resource slot load_resource is checking for overlap.
The party's timed effects, a table of 64 kept in the saved game. This first column holds each effect's kind, 0 for an empty entry; BOOT clears it ("PARTY SPELLS"). find_entry searches it.
The timed effects' second column: whom each one is on, a character slot, or a negative byte when it holds for any.

The timed effects' third column: the time left, its top two bits the unit (0 minutes, 1 ten-minute turns, 2 hours, 3 days) and its low six bits the count. age_effects_by counts it down, and one that would reach 0 is left at 1 with its unit bits cleared.
The party's square and facing in a 3D area ($49C0 across, $49C1 down, $49C2 facing), kept in the saved game: save_3d_position writes them and load_3d_area puts them back.
The party's overland square across.
The party's overland square down.
The area's map number, the GEO file LOAD FILES loads (or SQRDATA outdoors).

The game clock, seven figures counting up from here: $49C6 one this module never changes (it counts to 10), $49C7 minutes (to 10), $49C8 tens of minutes (to 6), $49C9 hours (to 24), $49CA days (to 30), $49CB months (to 12), then the year at $49CC/$49CD.
The clock's minutes, 0-9.
The clock's tens of minutes, 0-5.
The clock's hours, 0-23; $49CA days and $49CB months follow.
The year, low byte, which goes up when the months come round.
The year, high byte.
The locked door last given up on: its square's number (from the 3D driver, $C02A), for recall_door to recognise it.
The open-locks figure that last failed on that door.
The strength index that last failed to bash it.
The area that door is in, its map number.
The way the party faced that door.
The member chosen to speak in a PARLAY.
dungeon_init sets it to 0; nothing else in this snapshot reads or writes it.
Not zero in a 3D area (town or dungeon), zero outdoors: MOVE, the status line, AREA and the monster routines all choose by it.
One flag for each wall set, $49E7-$49E9: not zero leaves that set's characters as they are when its WALLDEF is installed (renumber_wall_chars).
When not zero, show_portrait shows nothing.
The days gone by, a 16-bit count (low byte; high at $49ED) that count_step adds to whenever the clock's days figure moves.
The days gone by, high byte.

The party's slowest movement, for check_flight.

ANIMATE (ANIMATE00, loaded at $8400 into resource slot 11) draws and animates the close-up pictures. Entry: a whole picture, or a portrait's body, from the header at $8C00 in the window whose top left is screen $CC7B (row 3, column 3), the 3D view's place.
Entry: draws the next frame of the picture on show (animate_frame_now, $8469). The modules call it once after each start and again on every pass of their key-waiting loops.
Entry: a portrait's body from $8C00 in the window at screen $CC44 (row 1, column 28), where LIBRARY's show_portrait puts a character's picture.
Entry: a portrait's head from $9000 in the window at screen $CC44.
Entry: a portrait's head from $9000 in the window at screen $CC7B.
Entry: the picture's header at A (low) and X (high), as set_picture ($842B). FINAL uses it with set_place_entry for its own pictures.
Entry: the kind in A and the window's screen address in X (low) and Y (high), as set_place ($841D).
0 for a whole picture or a body (11 rows; its 128 characters are cleared when it starts), 1 for a head (5 rows, drawn over the top of the body).
The colour RAM address of the window's top left (low byte; high at $8417), worked out by lay_out_codes from screen_place.
colour_place's high byte: the colour RAM row where the picture's colours start.

Where frames are built (low byte; high at $8419): $8755, 968 bytes of character patterns (121 characters), then 121 colour bytes at $8B1D. It lies past the end of the file, over the monsters' combat entries.
work_area's high byte, $87 for the frames built at $8755.
The screen address of the window's top left (low byte; high at $841B).
screen_place's high byte: the screen row where the picture's codes start.
$D0, the high byte of the character set. The picture's patterns go four pages above it, as characters $80-$FF.
Keeps the kind (A) and the window's screen address (X low, Y high).
Takes the header at $8C00, where BODY and PIC load, and carries on in set_picture.

Points $FD/$FE at the picture's header (A low, X high), blanks the window's colours (blank_window) and sets the high byte of shown_header to $FF, so that the next frame starts the picture from its first frame.
Kind 0 at $CC7B, header $8C00.
Kind 1 at $CC44, then the header at $9000, where HEAD loads.
Keeps the kind and place, then takes the header at $9000.
Kind 0 at $CC44, header $8C00.
Kind 1 at $CC7B, header $9000.
Draws a frame only when resource slot 5 (PIC, its file number at $6E18) or slot 13 (BODY, $6E20) holds a loaded file, a number below $7F. Then sets $6DDF to 1 and clears $6D78.
Fills the window's colour RAM with the background colour ($D021), so that it shows nothing while the picture is built: 11 columns by 11 rows for kind 0, 5 rows for kind 1 (window_rows).
The window's rows less one, by kind: 10 and 4.

Draws the next frame of the picture whose header $FD/$FE points at. A new window place lays the character codes out again (lay_out_codes). A new picture starts from its first frame (restart_picture); the same picture goes on to the next frame of its sequence, and after the last starts again.

A whole picture or a body clears its 128 characters, the four pages from charset_page + 4, before it starts. When they lie under the I/O area ($D000-$DFFF) the interrupts are held and bit 2 of $01 cleared, so that the writes reach the RAM there.
The high byte of this STA's address: draw_picture_frame sets it to charset_page + 4 and the loop steps it through four pages.
The operand of this LDA: 1 when the I/O area was switched out for the clearing and has to come back.
The same picture: header byte $33 is the place in the sequence. A sequence letter there means the next frame; 0 means the sequence has ended and the picture starts again.

Starts the picture: the sequence place (header byte $33) set to 0, the three background colours from header bytes $34-$36 into $D021-$D023, the codes laid out, the header kept in shown_header and the start of its frame changes (the header + $38) in stream_place, and the work area's 1089 bytes cleared.

Applies the next frame's changes from stream_place: first to the character patterns at $8755, then to the colours at $8B1D (apply_changes), and keeps the place where the following frame starts. Then waits until the raster is on lines $80-$9F and copies the patterns into the character set from character $80: header bytes $2F/$30 give the count, and the I/O area is switched out when the set lies under it.

Copies from the address at $862C/$862D to the address at $862F/$8630, index Y downwards. The branch at $8632 is rewritten: BNE ($D0) copies until Y is 0 again, a whole page when Y starts at 0; BCS ($B0), entered with carry clear, copies one byte.
The low byte of copy_page's source, set to work_area; $862D, the high byte, steps a page at a time.
The high byte of copy_page's source, one more for each whole page copied.
The low byte of copy_page's destination, set to 0; $8630, the high byte, starts at charset_page + 4 and steps with the source.
The high byte of copy_page's destination, from charset_page + 4, one more for each whole page.
The branch apply_frame rewrites: BNE ($D0) or BCS ($B0).
The operand of this LDA: 1 when the I/O area was switched out for the copy and has to come back.
Copies the colours from $8B1D into colour RAM at colour_place, header byte $2D to a row and header byte $31 in all.

The high byte of the colours' source.

The operand of this CPX: the number of colour bytes, header byte $31.

Holds the frame on screen. The sequence letter (A for the first) picks a delay from the header's table at $20; it is added header byte $2C plus one times, at most $FF, and the routine waits until the jiffy clock's low byte, $A2, has moved on that many ticks. Then the sequence place moves on by one.

Where the next frame's changes start (low byte; high at $86B5).
stream_place's high byte, in the XOR changes after the header.
The header of the picture on show (low byte; high at $86B7). A high byte of $FF makes the next frame start a picture afresh.
shown_header's high byte, the header of the picture on show.
The screen place the codes were last laid out at (low byte; high at $86B9).
shown_place's high byte, the frame of the picture on show.

XORs one stream of changes from ($FB) into the bytes at ($FD), in order, until a 0. Each control byte n: a positive n is followed by n bytes, one for each target byte; a negative n by one byte for the next -n target bytes, so a run of zero bytes skips them. Leaves ($FB) after the 0.
The operand of this LDA: the byte apply_changes XORs in, so that a run repeats it.
$FF while a run repeats one byte, 0 while each target byte has its own.

Writes the character codes $80, $81 and on into the window at screen_place, header byte $2D to a row, for header byte $2E rows, and works out colour_place, the same place in colour RAM, from the screen address's place within its 1 KB screen.

The rows lay_out_codes has still to write.
The work area's second page of character patterns, where copy_page's source pointed in the snapshot (apply_frame rewrites the operand for each page it copies).
The work area's colours, 121 bytes, one for each character of the 11 by 11 picture, which apply_changes alters frame by frame and copy_colours puts into colour RAM.

Where a HEAD file loads (slot 14), the portrait's head, with its own ANIMATE header, beside the body at $8C00.

A string buffer: decode_string unpacks a script's packed text here and input_line keeps a typed line here, which INPUT NUMBER and INPUT STRING read. draw_monster_sprites borrows its first bytes for a sprite picture's header (read_sprite_header copies twelve): $9700 and $9701 the two shared sprite colours, and later $9700 the image to stop at.
The sprite header's second shared colour, for $D026; then the sprite being set, counted from 1.

The sprite header's places, two bytes for each of the three distances ($9702-$9707), across then down, which draw_monster_sprites adds to each image's own offsets. Outdoors ($49E6 zero) it writes $8E across and $75 down there first.
The last place byte, distance 2's down. draw_monster_sprites also counts the image sets from here, from X = 1, when it adds up the sets before the distance wanted.
The sprite header's image counts, one for each distance ($9708-$970A): how many images the picture shows close, further and furthest.
The sprite header's twelfth byte, the picture's SPRITE file number, which find_sprite_picture compares with $6DD0.

The image to show next, counted over all the pictures held: find_sprite_picture leaves the found picture's first image there (12 for each entry), and draw_monster_sprites moves it on to the distance's set and then image by image.
The found picture's first image, kept so that each image's offsets can be found by its place in the picture (two bytes each from header byte $10).

FAST1.O, the game's fast loader, which BOOT loads to $B700. INIT, GEN and CAMP call this when the player kept the fast loader ($6DE5 = 0), after loading the drive's half of it, the file PIC64, to $8C00. It points the KERNAL's LOAD vector ($0330/$0331) at fast_load, sets CIA 2's port A directions ($DD02 = $3F), and writes 24 pieces of 32 bytes from $8C00 into the drive's memory from $0400 with M-W commands, then sets the M-W header back to $0400 and 16 bytes, ready for a file name.

The KERNAL's LOAD goes here. A verify ($93 not 0) or a name starting with "$" goes on to the KERNAL's own load ($F4A5). Otherwise the name is written into the drive at $0400, padded to 16 bytes with shifted spaces ($A0), and M-E starts the drive's code at $0410. The file then comes in 256-byte blocks (receive_block): a block whose first byte is negative is an error, returned with carry set and A = 4 (file not found) for the first block or 0 for a later one. The bytes go to the address in $C3/$C4 or, when the secondary address ($B9) is not 0, to the file's own load address; a link byte of 0 marks the last block, whose second byte is the index of its last byte. Returns with carry clear and the address after the last byte in X (low) and Y (high), the KERNAL's way.
Interrupts off; keeps the VIC bank bits of $DD00 in $02 and releases the serial lines, then waits for the drive's signal on DATA.
The BIT hides LDA #$00 at $B832: the first block's error enters at $B82F and returns 4, a later block's at $B832 and returns 0.
Copies bytes 2-255 of the block at $B900 to ($AE) and moves $AE/$AF on ($B839 copies from index X).
copy_fast_block from index X: fast_load's first block enters here with X = 4, past the link bytes and the load address.
Adds Y to the destination $AE/$AF.
LISTEN for the drive in $BA, then secondary address $6F, the command channel 15.

Receives 256 bytes from the drive into $B900. For each byte: waits for the drive's signal on DATA, keeps clear of raster lines from $32 where ($D012 - $32) AND 7 is 0 so that the VIC's stolen cycles do not upset the timing, releases CLOCK to start the drive sending, reads $DD00 four times on exact cycles, two bits (CLOCK and DATA, bits 6 and 7) each time, and pulls CLOCK again.
"M-W", the drive memory address (low $B8A5, high $B8A6) and the count ($B8A7), sent before each piece of drive code or the file name.
The M-W command's drive address, low byte: install_fast_loader moves it 32 bytes on for each piece of drive code, and leaves $0400 for fast_load's file name.
The M-W address's high byte, 4 for the drive's buffer at $0400.
The M-W command's count: 32 bytes for each piece of the drive code, then 16 for a file name.
Sent backwards from $B8AC: "M-E" and $0410, the address of the drive's code.
The block buffer, the 256 bytes receive_block takes from the drive. Its first byte is the next block's track: 0 in the file's last block, negative when the drive reports an error.
The block's second byte: the next block's sector, or in the last block the index of its last byte, where the copy stops.
In the file's first block, the file's own load address, low byte ($B903 high), used when the secondary address is not 0.
The first block's load address, high byte; the file's bytes follow from $B904.
The sprite pointers, after the screen at $CC00: one byte for each of the eight sprites, where $60 plus an image's number picks its 64 bytes from $D800 (draw_monster_sprites).
The view's character buffer, 11 rows of 11 (121 bytes): clear_view lays the sky, horizon and ground, the wall drawing covers them, and show_view copies the buffer to the screen.
One past the character buffer's end, where draw_cell's store pointed in the snapshot (draw_wall sets the operand and moves it 11 bytes a row).
The view's colour buffer, 121 bytes beside the characters, which show_view copies to colour RAM.
One past the colour buffer's end, where draw_cell's colour store pointed in the snapshot.

The sprite pictures' colours, one byte for each image (12 to an entry): the last byte of each 64-byte image, which load_sprite_picture copies here. Its low four bits are the colour and bit 7 makes the image multicolour.
WALLS (slot 9), in the RAM under the KERNAL: the characters of the three wall sets' five shapes, 780 bytes a set ($ED50, $F05C, $F368), then their colours from $F674, to $FF97.
The fourth shape of the first wall set's characters, 468 bytes into WALLS, where draw_cell's character source pointed in the snapshot.
The fourth shape of the first wall set's colours, 468 bytes into the colour part, where draw_cell's colour source pointed in the snapshot.
The KERNAL's SECOND, which sends a secondary address after LISTEN: the LIBRARY ($3FB8) and listen_command call it with the ROM in. The RAM beneath holds WALLS's last colours.
